findings.plain_summary: OPM is soliciting public comment through December 18, 2026, on a one-time Paperwork Reduction Act collection (OMB 3206-NEW) from tribal employers applying to join the FEHB Program. The collection would gather employer identity, representatives, key tribal personnel, billing unit and bank account information, and an employer profile, and OPM estimates 75 respondents at 2.25 hours each (168.75 total hours), none of which the summary mentions.

items.headline: Application collects bank account, billing, and key personnel data from tribal employers
items.what_changes: The one-time application would gather tribal employer identifiers and representatives, key tribal personnel, billing unit and bank account information, and an employer profile. The summary refers only generically to an information collection request and does not list these categories.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: This collection consists of information identifying the tribal employer and its representatives for FEHB purposes, key tribal personnel, billing unit and bank account information, and a tribal employer profile.

items.headline: Burden estimate of 75 respondents at 2.25 hours each
items.what_changes: OPM estimates 75 respondents will each spend 135 minutes on the one-time collection, for a total of 168.75 burden hours. The summary does not mention respondent counts or burden.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Estimated Time per Respondent: 135 minutes or 2.25 hours.

items.headline: Tribal employer eligibility defined by reference to specific statutes
items.what_changes: OPM's definition of tribal employer in 5 CFR 890.1402 covers tribes and tribal organizations running at least one ISDEAA or Tribally Controlled Schools Act program, and urban Indian organizations running at least one title V program. The summary does not describe who is eligible to apply.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: OPM defines ``tribal employer'' in 5 CFR 890.1402 to include an Indian tribe or tribal organization carrying out at least one program under the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act or the Tribally Controlled Schools Act; or an urban Indian organization carrying out at least one program under title V of the Indian Health Care Improvement Act.

items.headline: Enrollment eligibility follows employer election and employee status
items.what_changes: Once a tribal employer elects to participate under 5 CFR 890.1404, eligible common law employees become eligible to enroll under 5 CFR 890.1405, depending on employment type such as full-time or seasonal. The summary does not describe this sequence.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Once a tribal employer elects to participate in the FEHB Program in compliance with 5 CFR 890.1404, a tribal employee who is considered a common law employee and meets FEHB requirements for the type of employment (e.g., full-time, seasonal) will become eligible to enroll in FEHB pursuant to 5 CFR 890.1405.

items.headline: Comment period closes December 18, 2026
items.what_changes: Comments are accepted until December 18, 2026, under a 60-day notice process. The summary does not state a deadline.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Comments are encouraged and will be accepted until December 18, 2026.

items.headline: Collected information is not published
items.what_changes: OPM states that the information gathered through this application will not be published. The summary is silent on whether the data will be made public.
items.speaker: OPM

could_not_determine: How many tribal employers are currently eligible or expected to apply beyond the 75 respondent estimate
How many tribal employees would become newly eligible for FEHB enrollment once employers participate
The specific data fields, form questions, or format of the application itself
The methodology or assumptions behind the 135-minute per-respondent burden estimate
Whether respondents face any costs beyond the time burden, and the dollar value of that burden
How bank account and other sensitive information will be protected, stored, or used beyond what this notice states
The text of 5 CFR 890 subpart N, which this notice cites but does not reproduce
The timeline for OMB approval and any follow-on 30-day notice after the comment period closes
The number and content of comments received on any prior collection or pilot
